title: Census 2025 income, poverty, and insurance measures move on different household-security clocks
source_unit: Census Current Population Survey Annual Social and Economic Supplement (CPS ASEC) national income, poverty, and health-insurance estimates

denominator.unit: CPS ASEC household income universe; national estimate; release does not expose a single respondent denominator in the press summary

observations.method: Census 2025 Income, Poverty and Health Insurance release based on the 2026 CPS ASEC; the press release describes this as the highest real median household income in the series beginning in 1967.
observations.uncertainty: The press summary does not reproduce the full variance table or subgroup distribution. Median household income is not disposable income, liquid capacity, consumption, or equal household security.
observations.subgroup: All US households in the CPS ASEC income universe.
observations.counterinterpretation: A higher median can coexist with poverty, insurance gaps, unequal gains, taxes, debt, regional costs, and households below or above the median experiencing different changes.

denominator.unit: CPS ASEC official-poverty population universe; national estimate

child_official_poverty_rate.unit: percent of children; reported historic low

observations.method: Census Poverty in the United States: 2025, official poverty measure; pretax money income compared with family-size thresholds.
observations.uncertainty: The official measure excludes noncash benefits and tax effects and does not reproduce the full subgroup standard errors here. A rate change is not a household event or causal explanation.
observations.subgroup: All people for the 10.2% measure; children for the 13.4% measure.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower official poverty rate can coexist with higher post-tax or geographically adjusted hardship, medical costs, housing costs, or food insecurity for selected groups.

denominator.unit: CPS ASEC SPM population universe; national estimate

observations.method: Census 2025 SPM estimate incorporating taxes, noncash benefits, work expenses, medical expenses, and geographic housing-cost differences.
observations.uncertainty: Census reports the 2025 SPM rate was not statistically different from 2024; this record does not reproduce the full confidence interval or component contributions.
observations.subgroup: All people in the SPM universe.
observations.counterinterpretation: SPM and official poverty answer different questions; neither identifies a specific bill, benefit interaction, price, employer, or recovery path.

denominator.unit: CPS ASEC health-insurance coverage population universe; national estimate

observations.method: Census 2025 Health Insurance Coverage estimate from the 2026 CPS ASEC; full-year uninsured status is kept separate from poverty and coverage-at-any-time measures.
observations.uncertainty: Census reports the 2025 full-year uninsured estimate was not statistically different from 2024; the press summary does not reproduce subgroup standard errors or coverage duration detail.
observations.subgroup: All people in the CPS ASEC health-insurance universe.
observations.counterinterpretation: A national full-year coverage rate does not show underinsurance, network access, medical debt, care delay, premium burden, or whether a person could obtain care when needed.

related_sources.claim: USDA annual food-security prevalence and severity are separate household-security outcomes and are not replaced by income or poverty measures.
SHED supplies household-reported hardship and price-adaptation context that CPS ASEC national income and poverty measures do not identify.

boundary: This is a current national CPS ASEC release surface. It records income, official poverty, SPM poverty, and full-year uninsured estimates as separate measures. It does not establish household-specific purchasing power, a causal price or policy effect, benefit adequacy, medical access, trust, political action, or later recovery. No report PDF or microdata was acquired for this page-vintage record.
